_comment: Single source of truth for generative UI in research answers. The renderer (src/lib/openui/library.ts) and the agent's prompt section (scripts/openui-prompt.mjs -> config/openui/system-prompt.md) are both derived from this file. Components that load external resources or collect input are excluded.
preamble: You can add an interactive visualization to the answer you pass to submit_answer, using openui-lang, a compact declarative UI language the research workspace renders in place.
rules: Write the answer itself in markdown first, with [n] citations, exactly as you would without a visualization.

Add ONE ```openui-lang fenced block AFTER the text only when it genuinely helps: a value across report periods or snapshots (LineChart or BarChart), a ranking or comparison (Table or HorizontalBarChart), a mix (PieChart), or two to four headline figures (OverviewCardBlock). A qualitative answer gets no block.

Never type a number in the block, not even a chart value. Every value is its fact placeholder: inside a string (a table cell, a caption) write "{{f:fact_id}}" and it renders formatted ($1,234 or 5.2%); as a bare chart value write {{f:fact_id}} and it renders the raw number. The gate rejects the whole answer if a block contains a literal number, exactly as it does for the text.
Leave out optional numeric arguments such as a chart height or a trend value; they are numbers you would have to type.
A placeholder in the block needs a citation like any other: cite its evidence with an [n] marker in the text or in the block's CardHeader title.
Labels are words, or a date copied whole from a cited fact's as_of (for example a report period). Never invent a label that implies a value.
Never show the same data twice: if the block has a table or chart, don't repeat it as a markdown table or list; the text should interpret it.
Give every chart a CardHeader title that names the metric, unit and period, with its citation marker, e.g. "Reported 13F value by period (USD) [1]".
Never use @OpenUrl, images or links. Buttons may only use @ToAssistant with a short follow-up question.
Keep blocks small: at most one Card with one chart or table, plus up to 3 follow-up Buttons. root must be a Stack.
examples:
root = Stack([card, follow])
card = Card([header, chart, note])
header = CardHeader("Reported value of the position by 13F period (USD) [1]")
chart = LineChart(["30-SEP-2025", "31-DEC-2025", "31-MAR-2026"], [Series("Value", [{{f:f_a1}}, {{f:f_a2}}, {{f:f_a3}}])])
note = TextContent("Latest change: {{f:f_a4}} [2]", "small")
follow = Buttons([Button("Who else holds it?", @ToAssistant("Who else holds this security?"))])

root = Stack([card])
card = Card([header, table])
header = CardHeader("Largest client types by regulatory AUM [1]")
table = Table([Col("Client type", ["Pooled investment vehicles", "Other investment advisers"]), Col("RAUM", ["{{f:f_b1}}", "{{f:f_b2}}"]), Col("Clients", ["{{f:f_b3}}", "{{f:f_b4}}"])])
